articleTitle: Sixth International Conference on Metering Apparatus and Tariffs for Electricity Supply (Conf. Publ. No.317)
publicationTitle: Sixth International Conference on Metering Apparatus and Tariffs for Electricity Supply 1990

articleTitle: The software revolution in metering
publicationTitle: Sixth International Conference on Metering Apparatus and Tariffs for Electricity Supply 1990
abstract: High power microprocessor and memory systems are now readily available at low cost, and the electricity metering industry can now take full advantage of this with effective and well-planned software. The authors look at software methods and the product opportunities that software offers to meter manufacturers, and to designers of microprocessor and PC based electricity metering products and systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Traceability system of electric energy standard and tendency in static watthour meter development in Japan
publicationTitle: Sixth International Conference on Metering Apparatus and Tariffs for Electricity Supply 1990
abstract: The AC power standard in Japan has been established by the Japan Electric Meters Inspection Corporation (JEMIC) since 1964, and has been widely used as an electric power and energy standard for the electric power supply to industries. The authors describe the outline of the traceability system of the electrical energy standards and the technological trend and type approval regulation of the static watthour meters now in practical use.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Calibration of three-phase revenue meters under distorted waveform conditions
publicationTitle: Sixth International Conference on Metering Apparatus and Tariffs for Electricity Supply 1990
abstract: Increased awareness of the effect of harmonics on metering instrumentation has led to the establishment of a versatile three phase nonsinusoidal calibration system. Major North American meter manufacturers have already taken advantage of this facility to verify the accuracy of their new designs under distorted waveform conditions. Tests on existing meters have shown that energy meters are only moderately affected by the distortion. However, kVA maximum demand meters can exhibit very large errors. A need for inclusion in the national standard requirements limiting errors of the kVA demand meters operating under nonsinusoidal conditions is demonstrated.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Mains signalling-progress of a UK remote meter reading and load management system
publicationTitle: Sixth International Conference on Metering Apparatus and Tariffs for Electricity Supply 1990
abstract: The author describes the current evolution of a mains signalling spread spectrum two way communication system for remote meter reading and load management using the LV distribution network. Early development of the system was reported at the Mates 82 conference and the results of a 1000 house trial of the system was reported at Mates 87. The 1000 house trial has been followed by a contract placed by the UK Electricity Council to develop the system for volume manufacture and to manufacture 2000 sets of equipment for a pilot scheme for installation by the London Electricity Board. The author describes the stages of the development programme, the finalised specification of the equipment, detailed aspects of the system management and some of the design implications pertaining to the various national and international specifications the equipment has to meet.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A static domestic watthour meter based on Hall effect
publicationTitle: Sixth International Conference on Metering Apparatus and Tariffs for Electricity Supply 1990
abstract: The author lists the requirements for static domestic watthour meters. The author then discusses selection of the optimal metering technology. The author describes a single chip static meter based on a Hall sensor, including the ASIC. Future prospects for this type of meter are briefly discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: New metering and meter reading visions and decisions of the Helsinki Energy Board
publicationTitle: Sixth International Conference on Metering Apparatus and Tariffs for Electricity Supply 1990
abstract: The authors discuss the visions of the Helsinki Energy Board concerning the way the meters and metering systems ought to be improved. Further they look at the observations made when testing new technologies: experiences of hand-held terminals, experiences of the remote reading of meters by using the public telephone network and data over voice technology.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Statistical maximum demand measurement
publicationTitle: Sixth International Conference on Metering Apparatus and Tariffs for Electricity Supply 1990
abstract: The development of a statistical maximum demand meter and field tests carried out with the device are discussed, indicating that this method of maximum demand metering produces more realistic results than the thermal or block interval methods currently used, particularly when applied to rapidly varying loads. Commercial tariffing by this method is also discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design, benefits and flexibility in intelligent metering technology
publicationTitle: Sixth International Conference on Metering Apparatus and Tariffs for Electricity Supply 1990
abstract: The authors examine some of the technical features of the CALMU (Credit and Load Management Unit) microelectronic metering and communication technology focusing on the measurement algorithms, the hardware/software architecture, and the consequential operating flexibility and power of the CALMU system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Integrated semiconductor solutions for metering and telemetering applications
publicationTitle: Sixth International Conference on Metering Apparatus and Tariffs for Electricity Supply 1990
abstract: The conventional Ferraris electricity wheel meter has served the industry well over many decades as a basic instrument for measuring domestic power and is likely to survive for a good many more. However, multi tariffing systems to facilitate efficient load management will require the use of sophisticated semiconductor based solutions. As cost reduction considerations continue to drive system integration, the gradual replacement of the mechanical Ferraris wheel function by semiconductor devices is inevitable. The author briefly describes some design approaches based on microcomputers, and digital and linear ASIC technologies for the integration of such multifunction electricity measurement and telemetering systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A multi application contactless smart card applied to metering
publicationTitle: Sixth International Conference on Metering Apparatus and Tariffs for Electricity Supply 1990
abstract: The GEC Smart Card system is a significant advance in prepayment electricity meter technology. The contactless system greatly improves reliability by removing the need for physical contact with the internal electronics and the possibility of having no slots or apertures. Intelligence in the token allows multiple applications to be handled hence creating new opportunities from sharing the infrastructure or renting space on the card. Electronics for the token will be packaged in a standard sized plastic credit card. Use of a high level operating system and commands ensures compatibility with future upgrades in token or meters.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Metering data retrieval, a practical solution to the problem of inaccessible meters
publicationTitle: Sixth International Conference on Metering Apparatus and Tariffs for Electricity Supply 1990
abstract: The authors briefly discuss the problems of inaccessible meters and how electronics can overcome the problems. The authors discuss the EURIDIS project to develop domestic metering using a dedicated bus or pilot wire for communication between customers and utilities. The EURIDIS protocol specifications are briefly discussed and a technical description of the system is given. The services offered by this metering system are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Load research in a privatised electricity supply industry
publicationTitle: Sixth International Conference on Metering Apparatus and Tariffs for Electricity Supply 1990
abstract: The main distinguishing characteristic of load research is its focus on the time-related pattern of electricity usage, across the day and throughout the year. The authors describe how a major application for load research analysis is the design and setting of retail tariffs by distribution boards, and how an appreciation of the demand pattern throughout the year at customer class level is crucial for these tasks. Where new types of tariff are being contemplated, load research also plays a key part in helping to evaluate customer response.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Time of use pricing and two-way communications technology, SEQEB moves towards home automation
publicationTitle: Sixth International Conference on Metering Apparatus and Tariffs for Electricity Supply 1990
abstract: The South East Queensland Electricity Board is the third largest electricity distribution authority in Australia. The authors describe the implementation by the utility of a co-operative project which would enable the testing and evaluation of a computer-based telecontrol load management system, the development of administrative procedures, and the pilot testing of alternative domestic time of use electricity tariffs. The identification of desirable further developments in the equipment was also intended.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Multi function polyphase metering-an integrated approach
publicationTitle: Sixth International Conference on Metering Apparatus and Tariffs for Electricity Supply 1990
abstract: The authors concentrate on the design criteria of electronic multi function polyphase electricity meters, based on the operational requirements as perceived today and in the foreseeable future. Particular emphasis is placed on the measurement technique, data integrity, power supply design, display and communication features and design for reliability in use.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: New UK legislation, procedures, and practices for electricity meters
publicationTitle: Sixth International Conference on Metering Apparatus and Tariffs for Electricity Supply 1990
abstract: The Electricity Regulation Examining Service (ERES) became part of the Office of Electricity Regulation (OFFER) in 1989. In OFFER, the ERES has wider responsibilities but will continue to be involved in the pattern type approval of meters, certification of meters and the resolution of disputes concerning meter accuracy. These responsibilities are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Communicating with domestic electricity meters
publicationTitle: Sixth International Conference on Metering Apparatus and Tariffs for Electricity Supply 1990
abstract: The authors briefly discuss the latest developments in domestic electricity metering and then discuss meter communications systems for local, remote, and automatic meter reading. They describe optical links, pilot wire systems, power line carrier methods, telephones, and radio. The suitability and advantages of each type of system is discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Key budget metering-the total payment system
publicationTitle: Sixth International Conference on Metering Apparatus and Tariffs for Electricity Supply 1990
abstract: The authors briefly discuss the problems faced by London Electricity Board in relation to cash collection and debt problems connected with coin operated meters. The LEB decided to adopt key budget metering. The key is a two-way programmable device making it possible to credit the meter and to communicate information from the meter to the LEB. The authors discuss the key budget meter system and future development.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Remote reading and invoicing of EDF high voltage customers
publicationTitle: Sixth International Conference on Metering Apparatus and Tariffs for Electricity Supply 1990
abstract: The authors look at meter reading and invoicing of industrial customers of EDF who are supplied with HV or EHV. Metering 90 allows the reception of data from the customers, organised according to their tariff calendar, and the transmission of random tariff commands. Invoicing 90 allows various operations to be carried out monthly, these include: load curve calculations; energy consumption calculations; collection of payments; and generation of accounting entries.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Dynamic price structures and consumer load reaction
publicationTitle: Sixth International Conference on Metering Apparatus and Tariffs for Electricity Supply 1990
abstract: With the forthcoming reorganisation of the electric power industry in the UK, great interest is being shown in the likely relationship between suppliers and consumers in the new market scenario for energy sale and purchase. In an effort to improve utility economies, it is expected that greater use will be made of load management techniques, both direct and indirect. The use of dynamic or spot prices offers the means which is most consistent with market economics while still providing the utility with a Load Management alternative whenever necessary. The author examines the analysis and development of appropriate electricity tariffs and models for use within indirect load control strategies. These strategies use price messages to indicate to the consumer the actual costs and implications of his consumption of energy at the time it is required. In addition, consumer load models are presented. These, along with the price models, are used to estimate the optimal operating strategies of consumers.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Metering systems for energy management
publicationTitle: Sixth International Conference on Metering Apparatus and Tariffs for Electricity Supply 1990
abstract: Energy costs are frequently a major part of the overall running expense of a business and should be minimised. A clear understanding of how energy is being utilised is the first step to its control. The meter data base is created by recording for every meter on the system, the average demand in every demand period of the day. If transferred to a computer with mass storage capability, this data can readily be stored for a year or more and be available for processing and display by the user. In addition to the long term data storage of demand period data a short term 1, 2, or 3 minute average demand data store can provide information for a quasi-real time information system. By adopting the approach that utilities have taken for many years to their metering data a versatile tool for energy management is available.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Automatic acquisition and evaluation of metering data in the Saarland high-voltage network
publicationTitle: Sixth International Conference on Metering Apparatus and Tariffs for Electricity Supply 1990
abstract: The Vereinigte Saar-Elektrizitats-Aktiengesellschaft (VSE) is a regional electricity supply company in South-West Germany. The authors look at the automatic acquisition and evaluation of metering data in the Saarland HV network. Five areas are discussed in particular: acquisition of energy flows at supply points; remote transmission of the measured values to the dispatch centre; processing of measured values in dispatch centre and metering department; and evaluation with regard to economic energy management.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Electricity pricing for customer-utility optimisation of the supply of peaking power
publicationTitle: Sixth International Conference on Metering Apparatus and Tariffs for Electricity Supply 1990
abstract: The simultaneous and global optimisation of the customer's requirements for, and the power utility's supply of peaking power, remains one of the most challenging tasks of the tariff designer. It not only calls for integrated supply and demand side planning and tariff design, but also consideration of the decision making processes of the customer. The authors explain the benefits of centrally generated and coordinated generation of peaking power, identify the effects and symptoms of an incorrect price of peaking power, and then examine the possible approaches in electricity pricing to achieve optimality in the national supply of peaking power.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Coordinated electricity pricing and planning
publicationTitle: Sixth International Conference on Metering Apparatus and Tariffs for Electricity Supply 1990
abstract: An electricity industry consists of a supply side (the electricity supply industry, including third party generation) and a demand side (electrical equipment operated by consumers). Decisions about end-use requirements for heating, lighting, mechanical power and so on determine the demand for electrical energy, through the investment in and operation of electricity consuming equipment. These decisions are influenced by many factors, particularly electricity prices and their relationship to those of competing energy forms, such as natural gas. Consumer perceptions of environmental impacts may be increasingly important in the future. Countries around the world are searching for improved structures for national electricity industries that take into account recent developments. The authors outline a new planning and pricing framework for the electricity industry that would facilitate progress in these areas.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Energy transfer management system for invoicing services to independent power producers/users
publicationTitle: Sixth International Conference on Metering Apparatus and Tariffs for Electricity Supply 1990
abstract: The load data processing system described, set up for use with a personal computer, provides for efficient management of invoicing for services supplied by ENEL for certain types of user. The TMEN system has been devised to deal both with energy transfer users and with users with several consumption points covered by a single contract. In addition, the system could be used in the case of energy exchange between two utilities via the network of a third utility. When the system has been installed in all ENEL's outlying units that have to manage this kind of business, the result should certainly be speedier, more efficient invoicing. At the present time, the TMEN system is being tried out in the invoicing of a number of customers in Northern Italy.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The planning and installation of Norweb new meter station using automatic meter testing equipment
publicationTitle: Sixth International Conference on Metering Apparatus and Tariffs for Electricity Supply 1990
abstract: The authors discuss the planning and construction of the Norweb new test station for automatic meter testing. Automatic test equipment manufactured by Zera GmbH is looked at and a single phase testing system is described. Staffing, management and refurbishment of the building are also described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Research on real-time pricing of electricity
publicationTitle: Sixth International Conference on Metering Apparatus and Tariffs for Electricity Supply 1990
abstract: Electricity consumption in Finland varies quite strongly, according to seasons and times of day. However, it is possible to direct loads and to balance the fluctuation of electricity consumption and the authors show that tariffs are one such possibility of influencing load management. They describe how Imatran Voima Oy (IVO), the biggest electricity producer and wholesaler in Finland, has been investigating the possibilities of load management in its own R&D project. The project is concentrated on both direct and indirect control of load. As subjects of an investigation have been for example electric heating, load control possibilities of demand tariff customers and interruptible loads of industry.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Technology, measuring methods and measuring equipment for the repair and testing of electricity meters at a test board of a power supply enterprise
publicationTitle: Sixth International Conference on Metering Apparatus and Tariffs for Electricity Supply 1990
abstract: Test boards of power supply enterprises that are dealing with the repair and testing of electricity meters are often faced with a large variety of types in a relatively low number of units. The author looks at the testing of meters by Zahlerreparaturwerk Oranienburg (ZRWO). The five sections into which the maintenance and testing of meters are divided are: external cleaning; mechanical maintenance; adjusting; calibration; and standards board acceptance test.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The role of new metering technologies in combatting the greenhouse effect
publicationTitle: Sixth International Conference on Metering Apparatus and Tariffs for Electricity Supply 1990
abstract: For as long as humanity has lived on the Earth, Nature has taken care of our wastes. Through science and technology, we have discovered more and more ways to use energy. Our whole civilisation has been built upon easy access to energy. We are now receiving direct feedback from the Earth in the form of global warming, with all that this implies. As consumers, there are a hundred things we can do to save energy. What is lacking is the feedback system that can tell us how we are doing, and encourage us to do better. The author argues that the intelligent electronic electricity meter can provide this feedback. It may be just a small green box with flashing lights and digital displays, but the information it can give us may, quite literally, save the Earth.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The effect of distorted waveforms on a Class 2 sampling electronic polyphase meter
publicationTitle: Sixth International Conference on Metering Apparatus and Tariffs for Electricity Supply 1990
abstract: The increasing use of electronic load and speed control techniques, and the connection of various nonlinear loads is contributing to increased distortion of electricity supply waveforms. Whilst there may be little scope for improving the performance of a conventional meter under such conditions, there is every opportunity for electronic meters to be designed with an appropriate balance between cost and performance. The authors argue that the first essential for an electronic meter designer is to comply with those standards that either exist, or are being drafted, and to use some judgement with regard to conditions that may not yet have been defined at all.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Computer aided meter testing equipment for the certification and calibration of single phase tariff meters
publicationTitle: Sixth International Conference on Metering Apparatus and Tariffs for Electricity Supply 1990
abstract: The authors present computer aided meter testing equipment for the certification and calibration of single phase tariff meters. The equipment works by generating a signal when the black mark on the rotating disc passes through an infrared scanning head. The signal will trigger the count of pulses from the reference standard meter. The pulses from the meter and the reference meter are fed into the computer. The computer compares the number of impulses of the reference standard and the test meter to calculate the meter error.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: FLAG, a common communications protocol
publicationTitle: Sixth International Conference on Metering Apparatus and Tariffs for Electricity Supply 1990
abstract: The need for a protocol for reading and programming of metering has arisen from the wide variety of complex metering devices now available to the electricity boards. FLAG, a communications protocol, is invented to provide a common method of programming the sophisticated electronic metering equipment.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The evolution of a combined one or two element multi-rate, electronic kilowatt hour meter and radio teleswitch
publicationTitle: Sixth International Conference on Metering Apparatus and Tariffs for Electricity Supply 1990
abstract: Substantial experience of using discrete electronic products for control and measurement of domestic electrical load now exists within the United Kingdom Electricity Boards (or Distribution Companies). The authors briefly describe two of these products, one for metering and one for load control. They describe the evolution of a combined electronic kWh meter and radio teleswitch from tried and proven discrete products. The need for, and benefits of, combined two element metering and load control switching are discussed with particular emphasis on the use of this product as a tariff development tool. The combination of multi-rate metering, tariff control, load switching and communications in a single enclosure heralds the first generation of truly intelligent domestic meters.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Development of watthour meter based on a custom-integrated circuit
publicationTitle: Sixth International Conference on Metering Apparatus and Tariffs for Electricity Supply 1990
abstract: The authors discuss the requirement for and the development of a double register electronic watthour meter and a centralised telecontrol system. In particular they describe the custom IC and current sensors in the meter, and the radiofrequency and ripple control links in the telecontrol system. The equipment described is used for the double tariffing of small power consumers in Brazil.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The implementation and benefits of token metering in the East Midlands Electricity Board
publicationTitle: Sixth International Conference on Metering Apparatus and Tariffs for Electricity Supply 1990
abstract: The author discusses the problems of coin operated domestic electricity meters and the development of token meters to overcome the problems. The market research, field trials, and technical specifications are briefly discussed. The use of magnetic token meters in place of plastic token meters is discussed including the sale of tokens and automatic dispensers. The performance and benefits of token metering are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Experimental systems for tele-reading over the low voltage network
publicationTitle: Sixth International Conference on Metering Apparatus and Tariffs for Electricity Supply 1990
abstract: The authors describe a number of mains-borne metering systems and experiments, which have been key projects in an international research effort. This has involved collaboration with a number of academic establishments and distribution companies. The authors determine the characteristics required of software and hardware systems. The result of extensive research is a number of large networks throughout Europe. There is also a network of intelligent meters that can be configured as a portable vehicle for measurement studies of, line time domain noise intensity, communications efficiency and many other statistical parameters. Early studies of spread spectrum experiments and differential phase shift keying (DPSK) are reported, as these assisted in defining the development of a later system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Remote credit management-an alternative to prepayment meters
publicationTitle: Sixth International Conference on Metering Apparatus and Tariffs for Electricity Supply 1990
abstract: From the early days of electricity supply in the UK, certain users have required, and demanded, a 'pay as you go' system. Changing social conditions over the last ten years have made coin based systems increasingly less attractive so different types of prepayment systems are being introduced. The authors discuss the credit management unit (CMU) which uses a microcomputer to monitor payment.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Pricing of electricity for electrically under-developed areas
publicationTitle: Sixth International Conference on Metering Apparatus and Tariffs for Electricity Supply 1990
abstract: The authors describe Eskom's unique experiences underlying the design of price structures for low energy consuming urban and rural communities. They discuss the merits of various options or approaches to make electricity affordable to this segment of the market and describe the final choice of price structure. Finally, they describe some 'lowest acceptable cost' technology developments and discuss expected system effects and the impact on capacity expansion plans.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Managing the metering scene
publicationTitle: Sixth International Conference on Metering Apparatus and Tariffs for Electricity Supply 1990
abstract: The authors review the metering experiences of China Light and Power, Hong Kong. The Company continues to enjoy high annual growth rates, however, it was found prudent to strengthen the monitoring of existing meter installations. The authors include mention of tariff groups, metering controls, metering reliability, and some actual metering problems. They comment on prevention, detection and prosecution measures and in particular on computer assisted meter management, in the exercise of vigilance over some 16.8 million accounts issued each year and in the prompting of a visible presence on site at the 'high risk' meter installations.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: TIC: modernisation of metering apparatus and tariffing in a Belgian company
publicationTitle: Sixth International Conference on Metering Apparatus and Tariffs for Electricity Supply 1990
abstract: The author looks at the modernisation of the Belgian company Intercom SA with the use of a new SCADA system. The system has a local RAM memory, which stores data for a minimum of seven days, and an auto-answer modem for the public telephone. Real-time programs of the TIC software are integrated in the SCADA. The system has many functions including quarter hourly input, tariffing and statistical analysis.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: New metering equipment-Norweb's approval and implementation procedure
publicationTitle: Sixth International Conference on Metering Apparatus and Tariffs for Electricity Supply 1990
abstract: The authors outline Norweb's policy and experience in the assessment approval, introduction and service performance of new metering and associated equipment. Their general approach, has therefore, been to make themselves aware of new products and select those which they consider most attractive. They have carried out evaluation tests in their laboratory, and where necessary on site, and devices with satisfactory technical performance have been considered for purchase. In service reliability has been monitored and failures investigated at the laboratory before reference to the manufacturers.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Electricity tariffs in Norway. Lessons from the past and ideas for the future
publicationTitle: Sixth International Conference on Metering Apparatus and Tariffs for Electricity Supply 1990
abstract: The production, transmission and distribution of electricity in Norway are taken care of by some 300 utilities, mainly publicly owned. The large number of utilities leads to different types of tariffs, and to a variety of price levels to the consumer. The reason is that the cost of delivery p kWh is highly variable across the utilities. In order to decrease this variability and to improve the efficiency and quality of the service. The authors outline Norwegian governmental policy adopted in order to achieve these objectives.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Reliability and flexibility in automatic acquisition of metering values in a large Swiss electric network
publicationTitle: Sixth International Conference on Metering Apparatus and Tariffs for Electricity Supply 1990
abstract: Energie de l'Ouest-Suisse (EOS) is a company that produces and transports electricity at high voltage and coordinates energy exchange between different countries. The metering values acquisition and processing system, the control centre and the load frequency control system are all discussed with particular attention being paid to the automatic acquisition of metering values.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Integrated metering products
publicationTitle: Sixth International Conference on Metering Apparatus and Tariffs for Electricity Supply 1990
abstract: During the last 10 years, the UK in particular has become increasingly interested in the introduction of solid state products within the metering market. Whilst this trend has not been seen in the rest of Europe, the UK market has made great strides within the domestic single phase metering area. Today, the solid state domestic meter makes up some 40% of the total UK market and it is anticipated that this growth will continue for many years to come. Here, the author describes the use of microelectronics based meters for such applications.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: New generation test equipment for new generation kWh-meters
publicationTitle: Sixth International Conference on Metering Apparatus and Tariffs for Electricity Supply 1990
abstract: The trend with new generation kWh-meters is that they are no longer measuring just kilowatt-hours. More and more functions are incorporated into the traditional straightforward kWh-meter, so that it becomes a highly sophisticated energy measuring and evaluation system. This calls for meter test equipment that is able to check and verify all the functions and features of the kWh-meter. The meter test system described generates all output test values of voltage, current, power factor and frequency electronically. A simple keyboard entry gives efficient and accurate setting of any output value.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Development of the electronic metering apparatus at Tokyo Electric Power Company
publicationTitle: Sixth International Conference on Metering Apparatus and Tariffs for Electricity Supply 1990
abstract: The new tariffs which has been applied since January 1988 in Tokyo, Japan, have posed a problem due to the diversity of tariffs for seasonal/time-of-use consumption and methods of determining the contract demand based on real value. The electronic watthour meter has solved the problem. The authors deal with the outline of these tariffs and the function of the electronic watthour meter applied along with new tariffs.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The present state of integrated communication metering systems
publicationTitle: Sixth International Conference on Metering Apparatus and Tariffs for Electricity Supply 1990
abstract: The author looks at meter reading and standardisation using integrated communication metering systems. Direct local reading using the ZVEI protocol is also discussed. Readout of a load profile using a TARIGYR 600 with hand terminal, a TARIGYR 600 with TARICOM modem, and a TARIGYR 400 with data over voice telephone channel is presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Experience with multi-function metering for commercial and industrial tariffs
publicationTitle: Sixth International Conference on Metering Apparatus and Tariffs for Electricity Supply 1990
abstract: An initiative was launched by Eastern Electricity in 1983 under which a number of UK manufacturers were invited to tender for the development of a low-cost solid-state multi-rate unit containing an integral calender clock and opto input/output port for attachment to an existing domestic credit meter. Much of the specification produced for this device was common to the requirements of a multi-function unit (MFU) for large power metering applications and the launching of the project was a catalyst to the wider development of such devices. The authors discuss the design requirements of such meters, their testing and programming, installation and commissioning, field experience, metering and billing.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Meter certification in the factory and test station using AMTE
publicationTitle: Sixth International Conference on Metering Apparatus and Tariffs for Electricity Supply 1990
abstract: The advent of modern electronics and low cost computers has resulted in the availability of fully automatic and semi-automatic testing systems. This means that varying types of meters can be handled accurately and efficiently when calibrating and testing them in the factory. Automatic meter test equipment (AMTE) is described for meter certification.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The direct field sensor: a mature solid state metering technology
publicationTitle: Sixth International Conference on Metering Apparatus and Tariffs for Electricity Supply 1990
abstract: The trend towards solid-state solutions in electricity metering is well established. Many technologies have become available each with its claim to special suitability for particular applications but none has yet established itself as the successor to the once-dominant Ferraris metering element. The reason for this is that Ferraris metering elements were widely applicable to the whole range of prevailing market needs, whether for simple single-rate domestic devices or for the most complex polyphase devices with capabilities for reactive energy measurement and impulsing outputs. No solid-state technology was able to offer the same universal flexibility, but a breakthrough in the development of a Hall-effect based transducer has changed this. The new technology is known as Vertical Hall and it overcomes the hitherto practical difficulties, namely temperature, linearity and offset problems, which have excluded it from metering applications in the past. The authors describe the Vertical Hall devices in particular the direct field sensor.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An experimental prototype of a numeric energy metering unit for LV customers
publicationTitle: Sixth International Conference on Metering Apparatus and Tariffs for Electricity Supply 1990
abstract: ENEL has decided to research and to study a new microcomputer based meter for domestic consumers, suitable to be fully integrated within future metering units. The authors discuss the background to the project and the main objectives in the prototype design. The functional architecture and the hardware architecture of the meter are described. The measurement accuracy is discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Hall effect based electrical energy metering device with fraud detection and instantaneous voltage, current and power outputs
publicationTitle: Sixth International Conference on Metering Apparatus and Tariffs for Electricity Supply 1990
abstract: Hall effect devices have proven acceptance within electricity metering; specialist Hall multiplier devices having been demonstrated as being capable of meeting specification for static watthour meters. Commercial Hall devices have been available for some time at low cost that perform within specification as current sensors, and when coupled with developments in mixed analogue/digital ASIC technology can produce a cost effective energy meter with the bonus of partial fraud detection as opposed to simple reverse drive detection. The voltage and current waveforms are available prior to multiplication as requested by some countries. It has been demonstrated that a single phase 240 volt meter with a working range of 100 amps can be constructed with a basic resolution of watt seconds (joules). The current range is easily extended by conductor sizing or sensor positioning. The author describes the technology involved in a Hall effect meter.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: New concept for original register value transmission for metering applications
publicationTitle: Sixth International Conference on Metering Apparatus and Tariffs for Electricity Supply 1990
abstract: The author introduces a new concept called STOM (serial transmission of original meter values), whereby the meter delivers original register values to the data collection system, thus avoiding problems and providing the assurance that data integrity is being maintained. The concept includes new data concentrator (transcoder) terminals as well as further development of proven electronic meters. The author also provides some points of comparison between traditional pulse transmission and the new concept.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Upwards to a reliable bi-directional communication link on the LV power supplies for utility services: field tests in Belgium
publicationTitle: Sixth International Conference on Metering Apparatus and Tariffs for Electricity Supply 1990
abstract: There is an increasing interest in the use of a bi-directional communication link between the electricity distribution company and the LV consumers to implement for example load management and distribution automation. Installation of a local network, by use of physical links involve irresponsible costs. Using the LV power lines not only for energy distribution, but also as a communication vehicle is therefore a favourable solution. However, there are a lot of disadvantages involved. Mains signalling has the reputation of being unreliable due to the high noise levels and strange transfer characteristics which are strongly time and place dependent. The authors examine mains signalling and indicate how reliable bi-directional communication can be made by applying advanced communication and coding techniques in the frequency band of 10 kHz to 95 kHz. As an example remote meter reading, among the unlimited utility services, was used to test the communication system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: EMU-the Energy Management Unit
publicationTitle: Sixth International Conference on Metering Apparatus and Tariffs for Electricity Supply 1990
abstract: The energy management unit (EMU) is a multirate electronic meter designed to have communications facilities using radio teleswitch and telephone lines. It accepts pulses from gas and water meters, and can process these and electricity data to provide information which includes pricing to the customer on a separate display unit. It is currently the subject on an EEC supported demonstration project. The authors describe the purpose of the demonstration project, and the strategy for its implementation through stages of design and development of the unit, selection of customers for the field trial, installation of the unit and arrangements for collection of customer reactions during the trial.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Remote meter reading, load control and distribution system automation utilising SWD technology
publicationTitle: Sixth International Conference on Metering Apparatus and Tariffs for Electricity Supply 1990
abstract: The authors discuss the application of sequential waveform distortion (SWD) technology and products in the power system. The main features of the SWD system are: remote meter reading and load control of individual customers; automatic electricity fraud detection; automatic customer load surveys; integration of remote water and gas meter reading; control and monitoring of distribution system automation devices, such as regulators, reclosers, shunt capacitor, and protection devices; and vast feeder and customer database management. Also covered is an indication of the economics of implementing distribution system automation (DSA), in terms of potential cost savings or new revenue sources possible.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Innovations in the pricing and metering of wholesale electricity in New Zealand
publicationTitle: Sixth International Conference on Metering Apparatus and Tariffs for Electricity Supply 1990
abstract: As a result of the restructuring of the wholesale electricity industry, and of the recently implemented wholesale pricing structures, the environment for a competitive electricity market in New Zealand has been set. This has encouraged a more efficient electricity industry which will in turn better position the industry against its energy competitors. The authors describe how the corporatisation of the New Zealand's Electricity Corporation and the associated deregulation have therefore been extremely successful in achieving the efficiency goals of the New Zealand government.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
